memory_candidates.content: The 'known extension-loader gap' where new scripts/lib/*.sh or scripts/*.sh files fail to reach a deployed .claude/ tree, previously assumed to be an inherent limitation of copy_scripts for already-loaded extensions, actually root-causes to a missing entry in the extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array. check-extension-docs.sh already detects this (FAIL: script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts) but the fix -- adding the file to provides.scripts -- was not previously connected to the loader-copy symptom. Before reaching for a one-off manual `cp` workaround after adding a new script file, run check-extension-docs.sh first and add any missing provides.scripts entry; re-running deploy-headless.sh then deploys it correctly with no manual copy needed.

When a script sources a shared lib unconditionally at the top of a multi-subcommand CLI (e.g. task-lock.sh's acquire/heartbeat/release/check/reap/session-* dispatch), a missing/broken lib breaks EVERY subcommand, not just the ones that actually use it -- this is a strictly larger blast radius than the lib had before extraction, and can silently break isolated-temp-root test fixtures that copy the main script but not its new dependency (since the fixture never knew about the new dependency). Prefer a lazy loader function (idempotent, guarded by a loaded flag) called only at the specific call site(s) that need the shared code, so unrelated subcommands remain unaffected by the dependency's availability.

In jq, `generator | first` (a bare pipe into the `first` filter, which is defined as `.[0]`) is NOT the idiom for 'take the first output of a generator, or null if empty' -- it pipes EACH output of the generator through `.[0]` individually (erroring on a non-array output) and produces ZERO outputs, never a null fallback, when the generator itself yields nothing. The correct idiom, used consistently elsewhere in this codebase, is `[ generator ] | first`: wrap in an array comprehension first, then index -- `[][0]` is `null` in jq, giving exactly the desired null-on-empty behavior from a single evaluation. Also watch for the related bug: inside `map(select(. != $x and (($arr | index(.)) == null)))`, the `.` inside `index(.)` refers to whatever value is piped through `$arr |`, i.e. `$arr` itself, NOT the map element -- bind the element to a named variable first (`map(. as $el | select(...))`) before using it inside a nested pipe.
